# Infragravity motions

`nearshore.infragravity` | Low-frequency nearshore motions.

Parent: [Nearshore hydrodynamics](nearshore.md)

Papers: 8. Claims: 7. Equations: 1.

## Synthesis

**Well established.** Infragravity motions occupy frequencies below incident wind waves and arise through wave-group forcing, breakpoint variation and nonlinear transfers; they can dominate shoreline runup, harbor or inlet fluctuations and low-frequency surf-zone currents.

**Governing physics.** Bound long waves generated by group-scale radiation-stress gradients may release as free leaky or trapped edge waves; shoaling, reflection, breaking, bottom friction, directional spreading, bathymetric trapping, currents and rotational shear control their transformation and dissipation.

**Dimensionless parameters.** Controls include normalized infragravity energy or runup, surf-similarity and relative slope, wave-group bandwidth, directional spread, relative bar geometry, reflection coefficient, friction parameter, current-to-long-wave celerity ratio, relative water depth and vertical shear normalized by depth-mean velocity.

**Major equations.** Models use depth-integrated mass and momentum equations forced by radiation-stress gradients or phase-resolving nonlinear shallow-water/Boussinesq equations; modal decompositions distinguish bound, leaky and edge waves, while vertically structured theory augments depth averages with frictional shear and rotation.

**Typical methods.** Studies deploy pressure and vertically stacked velocity sensors, separate frequency and directional bands, estimate bispectra and energy fluxes, decompose modes, compare barred and unbarred transects, force phase-resolving models, close energy balances and validate runup, phase and vertical structure independently.

**Numerical models.** The set includes phase-resolving barred-beach and inlet simulations, reduced runup analysis and a theoretical vertical-structure extension. Depth-averaged solvers capture many long-wave transformations but omit observed water-column shear and rotation.

**Experimental datasets.** Reviewed evidence spans controlled runup cases over slopes 0.02-0.04, a modeled barred coastal field site, Albufeira Lagoon Inlet observations and modeling for 25-300 s motions, and Duck94 vertical current profiles around 0.005 Hz.

**Validated ranges.** Evidence covers selected plane slopes, one barred coast, one wave-dominated inlet and one Duck94 frequency band. The relative importance of leaky, trapped, current-blocked and vertically sheared motions is conditional on local bathymetry and forcing.

**Recent advances.** Recent advances use dense arrays, remote sensing and distributed pressure sensing, three-dimensional and nonhydrostatic solvers, mode-resolving data assimilation, machine-learned surrogates and coupled infragravity–morphodynamic prediction.

**Disagreements.** Competing generation descriptions emphasize bound-wave release, breakpoint forcing or nonlinear energy transfer, and observed energy may combine gravity and vortical modes. Depth-averaged agreement in surface elevation does not prove velocity or sediment-transport accuracy.

**Limitations.** Sparse low-frequency records, finite deployments, directional ambiguity, sensor noise near boundaries, uncertain friction and bathymetry, mode leakage, nonstationary storms, current interaction and limited vertical arrays constrain attribution and transferability.

**Open questions.** Priorities include unified gravity-vorticity separation, three-dimensional structure, current blocking and Doppler effects, reef and headland trapping, sediment suspension, compound surge interactions, climate dependence and operational assimilation of low-frequency observations.

**Seminal papers.** Longuet-Higgins and Stewart linked wave groups to bound long waves; breakpoint-forcing and edge-wave theories explained surf-zone generation and trapping, followed by field bispectral studies and nonlinear phase-resolving models.

## Equations

### Spectral-spread infragravity-runup fit

$$
R_s^{ig}/(H_{s,0}L_0)^{1/2}=-0.013\ln[(f_p/f_s)\sigma_{\theta,0}]+0.058
$$

Regime: Idealized matrix with 0.6<(fp/fs)sigma_theta0<30.

Variables: `Rsig` significant infragravity runup; `fp` peak frequency; `fs` frequency spread; `sigma_theta0` deep-water directional spread

Source: (Guza 2012, [doi:10.1029/2012gl051959](https://doi.org/10.1029/2012gl051959))

## Claims

- **C95.** Over slopes 0.02-0.04, normalized infragravity runup showed no obvious slope dependence and was controlled more strongly by frequency and directional spread. *Regime: Limited moderate-slope, mostly dissipative simulations; not evidence of slope independence outside 0.02-0.04..* [direct_finding, numerical] (Guza 2012, [doi:10.1029/2012gl051959](https://doi.org/10.1029/2012gl051959))
- **C364.** At the modeled barred field site, infragravity energy was generally dominated by leaky waves, but outer-bar trapped edge waves contributed up to 50% of infragravity variance in mild conditions; shoreward losses shifted among nonlinear transfer, bottom friction, and breaking. *Regime: Gently sloping barred beach across mild and storm conditions represented by a validated local wavefield..* [direct_finding, numerical] (Dirk P. Rijnsdorp 2015, [doi:10.1002/2014jc010450](https://doi.org/10.1002/2014jc010450))
- **C368.** At Albufeira Lagoon Inlet, observed and modeled 25-300 s infragravity motions were blocked during ebb by opposing currents reaching 2.5 m/s, while flood-period fluctuations temporarily reached 100% of the background current magnitude. *Regime: Albufeira Lagoon Inlet observations and simulations, including opposing ebb currents to 2.5 m/s..* [direct_finding, mixed] (Xavier Bertin 2016, [doi:10.1002/2015jc011444](https://doi.org/10.1002/2015jc011444))
- **C1131.** A theory motivated by Duck94 observations extends depth-averaged low-frequency nearshore dynamics to represent vertical structure associated with frictional and rotational effects. *Regime: Duck94 barred surf zone near 0.005 Hz.* [direct_finding, analytical] (Lippmann 2016, [doi:10.1175/jpo-d-16-0015.1](https://doi.org/10.1175/jpo-d-16-0015.1))
- **C1132.** Duck94 observations near 0.005 Hz showed significant vertical structure in low-frequency surf-zone current energy, phase and rotation: cross-shore flow decayed toward the bed, while the weaker alongshore component could increase near the bed. *Regime: Duck94 barred surf zone near 0.005 Hz.* [direct_finding, field] (Lippmann 2016, [doi:10.1175/jpo-d-16-0014.1](https://doi.org/10.1175/jpo-d-16-0014.1))
- **C1371.** Infragravity transport contributed below 20% on a 1:35 beach but reached about 60% during energetic conditions on a 1:80 beach; HIG/HSW indicated suspension mechanism, direction and relative importance. *Regime: Cross-shore sand transport by infragravity waves as a function of beach steepness.* [direct_finding, field] (Anouk de Bakker 2016, [doi:10.1002/2016jf003878](https://doi.org/10.1002/2016jf003878))
- **C1372.** Bispectral laboratory analysis shows shoaling transfers energy from spectral peaks to harmonics and infragravity waves, while nearshore infragravity interactions dominate and cascade energy toward dissipative high frequencies. *Regime: Nonlinear Infragravity–Wave Interactions on a Gently Sloping Laboratory Beach.* [direct_finding, experimental] (Anouk de Bakker 2014, [doi:10.1175/jpo-d-14-0186.1](https://doi.org/10.1175/jpo-d-14-0186.1))
